title: Overton's Tennessee courts
text: John Overton served on Tennessee's Superior Court from 1804 to 1810, then on its Supreme Court of Errors and Appeals from 1811 to 1816. These were Tennessee courts; he was not a justice of the United States Supreme Court.

title: The Tennessee Reports
text: Overton and Thomas Emerson published the first two Tennessee Reports volumes in 1813–1817. The reports collected decisions of Tennessee's highest courts.

title: The archival Overton Papers
text: The Tennessee State Library and Archives finding aid describes the Murdock Collection of John Overton Papers as correspondence and other records, including legal and land business. Overton's papers are not the title of a single law book.

title: Travellers Rest and enslaved labor
text: Travellers Rest's museum describes the house as built through the labor of hired overseers and enslaved African Americans. Overton's legal career and wealth cannot be separated from slavery. An imagined modern reflection is not evidence of a historical conversion or repentance.

title: Harvey: research and human verification
text: Harvey describes legal research that retrieves authoritative legal sources and presents citations lawyers can open. Its account keeps the lawyer responsible for checking authorities and conclusions. This is Harvey's description of its workflow, not an independent test or a claim of infallibility.

title: OpenAI's dated Astra announcement
text: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra announcement describes computer use, software engineering and professional work. The page's September 29, 2026 update points to GPT-6.1 Sol. Astra is therefore not established as the latest model by this notice. These are vendor descriptions, not this portfolio's measured performance.

title: Anthropic's Opus 5.5 notice
text: Anthropic describes Claude Opus 5.5 as improving coding, computer use, cost and speed, with additional safeguards. Its performance comparisons are Anthropic's own claims and depend on the evaluation and settings; this card establishes no universal winner.

title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon rollout notice
text: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon announcement describes phased access, beginning with selected cyber defenders and then trusted partners. The notice does not establish broad developer or consumer availability. Announcement, access and a visitor's account eligibility are different questions.

title: Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 and API notice
text: Meta announced Muse Spark 1.1 and a public preview of its Meta Model API. It describes coding, reasoning and multimodal capabilities. API access alone does not establish open weights, a particular license, or that Meta's strategy can be summarized as Llama and open source.

title: Google's training and inference chips
text: Google describes TPU 8t as optimized for training and TPU 8i for inference, including agent workloads. Training a model and serving answers place different demands on compute and memory; the announcement is a vendor account of the designs.

title: IEA's dated data-centre electricity forecast
text: The IEA's 2025 Energy and AI release projected worldwide data-centre electricity demand of around 945 TWh in 2030, more than double its 2024 level. This is a dated projection for all data centres, not measured 2030 consumption and not AI alone.

title: Stargate: planned and operating capacity
text: OpenAI's January 2026 Stargate Community notice said its first Abilene site was training and serving systems while other sites were under development. Its planned capacity is distinct from operating capacity. Buildings, electricity, water and local infrastructure belong in the account of AI.

title: Micron's HBM packaging plans
text: Micron's January 2025 announcement scheduled operations at its Singapore HBM advanced-packaging facility for 2026 and meaningful capacity expansion from 2027. That announcement does not establish whether the facility opened on schedule. Memory packaging is a physical supply-chain dependency, not merely a software choice.

title: Anthropic's shared compute suppliers
text: Anthropic states that it trains and runs Claude on AWS Trainium, Google TPUs and NVIDIA GPUs. Competitors can also be infrastructure suppliers. Its future capacity agreements do not by themselves establish installed or operating capacity.
